newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW - Piltel sees recovery with fraud buster.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Piltel sees recovery with fraud buster.

text.p: Cellular phone operator Pilipino Telephone Corp (Piltel), battling against fraudulent calls, is to launch a marketing offensive after it has shielded its network from cloning, its president said on Tuesday.
"We are tearing down a lot of unauthorised calls," president Ramon Cojuangco told Reuters during an interview.
Piltel in 1996 allocated 886.35 million pesos ($31.3 million) for doubtful accounts largely due to cloning compared with 80.93 million pesos it allocated in 1995.
Most of these calls came from the central Visayas and southern Mindanao regions, Cojuangco said.
In this type of fraud, a phone number is copied and the charges are dumped on the legitimate holder of the number.

Cojuangco said Piltel was installing several anti-fraud measures, including advanced digital technology to protect its subscribers and the adoption of a personal identification system for all subscribers, besides imposing a credit limit on calls.
It has also adopted a "finger printing" system that effectively stops cloned phones from getting through the Piltel network.
By the end of August, Piltel plans to adopt another system that would allow subscribers to open or shut their access to the Piltel network, further minimising cloning, Cojuangco said.
"With all the features that we are putting in place, we are seeing a significant reduction in terms of incidences and amounts of cloning."

Cojuangco said Piltel planned to market aggressively its products once it had fully adopted new technologies and installed the software and hardware that would make it extremely difficult for cloners to penetrate its network.
"We are very hopeful all of these measures are going to be effective, thereby improving our service," he said.
Cojuangco said Piltel had slowed down its marketing in the first half of the year while building several layers of defence against cloning.

"We allowed ourselves to step back and not to be aggressive because we wanted to make sure that our backroom facilities and our costs would be able to sustain the next push in the second half of the year."
Cojuangco said his firm's adoption of new technology to combat cloning and the entry of a new shareholder would enable Piltel to recover sooner.
International phone gateway operator Philippine Global Communications Inc (Philcom) recently acquired a 20 percent stake in Piltel for $200 million.
As part of the agreement, Piltel has the option to acquire 20 percent of Philcom. Piltel has yet to exercise this option.
"Slowly we are recovering. Judge us in the fourth quarter," Cojuangco said.
Piltel, a unit of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, posted a net income of 42.6 million pesos in the first quarter of the year, sharply down from the year-ago figure of 246.6 million.

Early this year, Piltel said it expected to post flat profits in 1997 in the face of its cloning problems. It registered a net income of 710.47 million pesos in 1996 compared with 822.075 million the previous year. ($ = 28.35 Philippine Pesos)
